title: Decode IDs into text
summary: Decoding maps known token IDs back to text. Tokenization may not preserve every detail of original spacing, so test exact-text needs carefully.
introduction: Decoding maps known token IDs back to text. Tokenization may not preserve every detail of original spacing, so test exact-text needs carefully. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Decoding maps known token IDs back to text. Tokenization may not preserve every detail of original spacing, so test exact-text needs carefully.

blocks.code:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel({"[PAD]": 0, "[UNK]": 1, "moon": 2, "glows": 3}, unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
print(tokenizer.decode([2, 3]))
blocks.title: Decode IDs into text

blocks.text: The output is moon glows. IDs 2 and 3 map back to their words. This does not prove the original spaces or formatting can always be recovered.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not assume encode and decode preserve every input byte for all tokenizer settings.
